findings.F1: Failed breakouts were followed by rises, not falls: over 605 cases, the 5-day move after the signal was +0.19 % above the coin's drift (t 0.44), and +0.77 % in total. A short therefore lost about four times the 0.19 % cost of a trade on average, and the book's mean daily return was -0.028 % (Sharpe -0.49, against a required mean of at least 0.05 %).
findings.F2: The grading runs against the idea: a larger peak excursion above the old high brought a larger 5-day rise (slope +0.0022 of return per percent of excursion, t 2.53, 605 cases). The top excursion quintile (median 10.3 %) rose +1.02 % above drift, against +0.03 % for the bottom quintile (median 1.4 %).
findings.F3: The day right after the signal rose on average (+0.40 %, t 2.25, 605 cases), so the short entered just before a bounce.
findings.F4: The rise was strongest when the coin was already deep below its 60-day high. In the deepest quartile (median -22 %), the move was +1.81 % above drift (t 2.01, 128 cases), against about -0.1 % to -0.3 % in the other three quartiles. Neither the coin's 60-day return (slope t 0.34) nor its 20-day return (slope t 1.78) turned the sign negative in any quartile.
findings.F5: Only breakouts made on thin volume failed into a decline. When the breakout day's volume was in the lowest quartile against its 20-day average (median 0.63×), the coin fell 1.45 % below drift over 5 days (t -1.91, 125 cases), about 7.6 times the cost of a trade. The higher-volume quartiles rose +1.50 %, -0.30 % and +1.78 % (slope of the move on volume ratio +0.0094, t 1.89, 500 cases).
findings.F6: The short worked only in some years. The move was -2.97 % below drift in 2018 (t -1.85, 40 cases) and -2.25 % in 2019 (t -1.96, 65 cases), but +2.76 % above it in 2020 (t 2.97, 97 cases). No window carried the book: its mean daily return was negative in 11 of 24 windows.

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above its prior 20-day high, reaches further above it within the next 3 days, and then closes back below the old high, the coin falls over the next 5 days, only when the breakout day's volume was low against its 20-day average volume, and the lower that volume ratio was, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: Short failed breakouts whose breakout day traded thinly, and refuse those whose breakout day traded heavily, because heavy-volume breakouts that slip back below the old high tend to recover.
ideas.name: thin-volume breakout failure decline
